# R394 — historical prefill/decode performance regression audit

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Read-only review of Git benchmark reports, selected closed records/research notes and the current upstream bench.sh phase-cache result. No build, test, GPU/model/service/process access, cleanup, or Git operation was performed. No active Main/4331 log or protected `prefill-gemm-only-contract-root-v1/record.json` was opened. This report is the only new write.

## Finding

The current stock-client result is not evidence of a broad source regression. It measures Arc B570 / Ryzen 5600X / IQ3_S, exact actual prompt 32,049 tokens and 24 output tokens, with prefill 362–387 tok/s and decode 7.1–9.1 tok/s. A separate earlier closed quiet B570 production comparison at 32,768 + 16 reports decode 8.10 vs 8.27 tok/s across three samples per side; that overlaps the present short decode range and is expressly not attributed to its prefill-only change. The examined record set does not support a historical B570 decode result near 70 tok/s. The tempting 45–82 tok/s figures are from a different Windows RTX 5070 / ready-made 0.1.26 engine, MTP-enabled 256-token runs, and cannot be compared to this B570 source-built no-MTP work.

No confidently causal source/option regression from a prior B570 performance winner to the current bench.sh result is established by these records. The clear measurement-method change is custom GEN to pristine upstream `bench.sh --long --runs 3`: the latter produces a fresh ~32K prompt and caps each completion at 24 tokens, while custom GEN records longer continuations / different state and timing. These are distinct workloads. Current ON-vs-OFF phase-cache samples are a matched stock-client comparison for cache setting only, not a before/after source comparison.

## Read records and exact samples

1. Current comparison: `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-phase-cache-stock-bench-20261013/bench/results/2026-10-13-upstream-benchsh-phase-cache-pair/REPORT.md` and `summary.json` (individual source rows are in `upstream/results.json`; OFF rows are retained in summary). The report records source-built DPC++ 7.1.1, native IQ3_S, Arc B570 / Ryzen 5600X, context 262,144, KV resident 32,768, int8 KV, chunk 8,192, group16, workers5/tasks18, COPY0, no borrow/MTP/reuse, tracing/validation off, same binary/argv/model/client, only `STRATA_PHASE_DECODE_CACHE` changed. Every request read 32,049, reused 0, generated 24. OFF prompt samples 384.8, 383.1, 386.9 (median 384.8); decode 7.3, 7.8, 8.6 (median 7.8). ON prompt 362.4, 375.4, 383.0 (median 375.4); decode 7.1, 8.2, 9.1 (median 8.2). OFF then ON was sequential; ranges overlap and ON trends upward. No adoption; no full-context/quality qualification. `summary.json` explicitly says stock-long comparison eligible but strict 32768 threshold not met.

2. Prior B570 quiet production A/B: `/home/yayoi/.local/state/strata-sycl/post-reboot-tuning-20261007/research-20261009/research-current-prefill-measured-ledger-next-step-round313-v1.txt` and `research-current-decode-measured-ledger-next-step-round314-v1.txt`, which identify committed source records `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-prefill-gated-region-alias-20261013/bench/results/2026-10-12-decode-criticalpath-native-dequant-batch/README.md` and `results.json`. The archived reports state same 32K+16 setup, three clean samples per side, exact token/LP5 and healthy normal close: prefill 359.02→376.42 tok/s; decode 8.10→8.27 tok/s. Decode was unchanged by this prefill-only batch option and the report forbids attribution. Thus this is useful near-current performance context, not a causal decode improvement/regression. A separate diagnostic line at 124.09 ms/window came from validation-overhead timing and is performance-ineligible; do not convert it into TPS or compare with quiet request-rate samples.

3. Earlier high-looking public report: Git `bench/results/2026-09-29-speed-0126/README.md` and `matrix.json` were read. They are RTX 5070 12GB / Ryzen 7600 / Windows 10, ready-made 0.1.26 engine, five models and one run per cell, shipped `--prefill auto`, expert cache auto, KV streaming at long contexts, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`, greedy 256-token continuation. For IQ3_S: prompt rates 426.6 / 912.99 / 1624.07 / 1640.34 / 1443.21 at 1K/4K/32K/64K/128K; decode 52.4 / 53.3 / 48.31 / 46.25 / 45.51. Q2_0 decode reaches 81.75 at 32K. README calls decode the same as earlier 0.1.22 and notes single-run draft acceptance variation. It is not this Intel SYCL binary/device/model recipe or timing harness; it cannot establish a B570 regression. The official published values are the best old-looking numbers found, and their configuration explains the mismatch.

4. A newer stock bench method audit, `/home/yayoi/.local/state/strata-sycl/post-reboot-tuning-20261007/research-20261009/research-upstream-benchsh-decode-measurement-round342-v1.txt`, states pristine v0.1.43 `--long` is calibrated about 32,768 input, max 24 output, fresh prompt each request; actual reads must be used, and decode rates are short-horizon aggregate engine timers. It explicitly cannot represent sustained decode with a 32K prefix. This matches the 24-token current rows and explains why they are not equivalent to the historical custom GEN horizon.

5. The gated alias candidate report `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-prefill-gated-region-alias-20261013/bench/results/2026-10-13-gated-region-alias-diagnostics/REPORT.md` documents memory/fit/correctness diagnostics only, not speed. The overlay remains opt-in OFF; it must not be named as an observed speed regression or gain. The current phase-cache report likewise records that its candidate head-alias/12K source was unqualified and not executed in this measurement.

## Comparability assessment

| Evidence | Context/work | Hardware/source and mode | Relation to current 32,049 + 24 stock row |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Current phase cache OFF/ON | read 32,049, fresh, 24 generated | B570, free DPC++7.1.1, IQ3_S, stock client, no MTP | Matched for cache-only arm; small sample / sequential drift caveat |
| Prior native-dequant-batch A/B | 32,768 + 16 | B570, source 0691bcdf, no MTP; three quiet samples/side | Close context; decode 8.10/8.27, but no decode code/option change and not attribution |
| RTX 5070 0.1.26 README | 31,566 + 256 for 32K row | Windows, NVIDIA ready-made engine, MTP spec4, one sample | Not comparable: platform, engine, speculative decoding, horizon and timing method differ |
| Instrumented decode timing | 32,768 + 16 | B570, same source family, validation timing enabled | Ineligible diagnostic; not throughput baseline |
| Gated alias diagnostic | 1,024 / 32,768 requests | candidate diagnostic, not speed harness | No speed sample; no inference |

The user-recalled “near 70 tok/s” target plausibly aligns with the older discrete-GPU report's model/context/spec behavior, but the reviewed local reports do not identify it as a measured B570/source-built custom GEN sample. Do not silently discard a valid custom GEN record: its use must be classified by exact per-request read/reuse, generated count, timer definition, model bytes, binary/source, context/KV, MTP/draft acceptance, and full argv. Those fields are not available in the records read here, so the custom GEN result remains unclassified and cannot be folded into the current median. No number has been inferred for it.

## Chronology and causal status

- 2026-09-29: public `0.1.26` Windows/NVIDIA result, MTP spec4, 256 generated tokens; different platform and measurement setup.
- 2026-10-12: B570 source-built `0691bcdf` quiet 32K+16 comparison, prefill-only native-dequant batching. Prefill changed 359.02→376.42; decode 8.10→8.27 with no decode-path change; not a decode attribution.
- 2026-10-13: harness switched to pristine upstream `bench.sh --long --runs3`, which caps output at 24 and observes 32,049 rather than 32,768 actual input. Matched cache OFF/ON campaign changed only phase-cache environment; source/binary/model/client held. No evidence this method switch is a source regression, and its ON median decode does not show loss relative to OFF.
- Later gated-region alias source is a candidate, default OFF, and the reports show diagnostics rather than throughput. Therefore it cannot explain current baseline.

A true source/option regression remains possible only if a prior custom GEN record with comparable device, binary lineage, exact work, decode mode and timing is found. The selected evidence does not show which change could have caused one; naming CPU flags, COPY queue, cache policy, kernel, or aliasing as culprit would exceed the data.

## Minimum matched verification to recover the old result

After current run closure and under the measurement owner, use one frozen B570 host, same IQ3_S bytes/provider, same compiler/binary build recipe, same source revision where possible, same 32K+ prompt token IDs, context/KV residency, cache/read/reuse state, prefill chunk, COPY, CPU flags/affinity/workers/tasks, batch, MTP/drafter/spec settings, greedy sampling, and exact custom-GEN timing definition and output length. First reproduce the historical custom GEN workload with at least three fresh-process samples, retaining every individual sample, actual read/reused and generated counts, prompt/decode timers, correctness IDs/hash and faults/quit. Then run the stock `bench.sh` workload separately, clearly labeling its 32K/24-token limit. For source chronology, bisect only the smallest known source delta after the historical passing revision while keeping options fixed; compare one source change at a time. If exact old GEN inputs/config/binary identity cannot be recovered, report the old record as non-comparable rather than attempting a numeric adjustment. No tests or runs were performed for this audit.
